reason: In the FNA format 'Plants L × W dm' the first range is the height. 1-3(-3.5) dm converts to 10-30 cm with an extreme of 35 cm.

target: vascular bundle (PO_0005020) present, whole/container = fruit (pod); better: fruit with conspicuous veins
fix: 'venose' on an organ: the veins belong to that organ (here the pod), so keep the organ as the container. Also, 'venose' means the veins are conspicuous, not just present.
reason: Without the pod as container, 'vascular bundle present' says nothing about the taxon and is not what the flora says.
'Flexuous' (bending to and fro) is close enough to sinuous. 'More or less' is kept as 'approximately'.
'12-18 cm long and broad': the length of the leaf (blade) is 12-18 cm. The width is a separate annotation.
The stipules are adnate to the petiole. The target part is right.
'base cuneate' in a leaf-blade sentence: leaf lamina base is cuneate.
Cymules (cyme inflorescence) are few-flowered: flowers present, amount 'few', with the cyme as container.
The second range of 'L x W' is the width: 1.5-2.2 mm.

target: ovate (FLOPO_0991024) or [ovate (FLOPO_0991024) + leaf lamina base heart shaped (PATO_0000948)]
fix: A compound like 'ovate-cordate' is a shape plus a base: an ovate outline with a cordate base. Do not reduce it to plain 'heart shaped' for the whole blade.
reason: The second alternative loses its ovate outline and moves 'cordate' from the base to the whole lamina.
Oblong (PATO_0000946) to subelliptical (PATO_0005004): a range between two shapes.
'Seeds ... numerous': seeds present, amount 'many'.
8-13 secondary veins on each side of the midvein. The count and its position are both captured.
In Aquilegia 'blades' here are the petal blades, which are oblong or spatulate.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) on the leaf lamina, yellow (golden), stage young (PATO_0000309)
fix: 'golden villous' / 'ferruginous-tomentose' and similar: the colour word describes the hairs, not the surface they cover. Put the colour on the trichomes, and the hairiness (villous) on the part.
reason: The golden colour is that of the villous hairs, not of the leaf blade.

target: the pulvinate ring on the basal half of the calyx lobe is yellowish
fix: 'X with yellowish Y': the colour belongs to Y (the ring), not to X.
reason: Only the semicircular ring on the lower half of each lobe is yellowish, not the calyx.

fix: In descriptions of separate male and female flowers ('Male flowers ...; stamens 4'), carry the flower sex into the whole/state slot.
reason: Pilea has separate male and female flowers. Female flowers have no stamens, so 'stamens 4' without 'male flower' is false.
A drip-tip 1.5-3 cm long is a caudate apex, and 'often' is kept. 'On sterile shoots' is only a qualifier, and 'often' already covers it.
'Herbs perennial': whole plant has a perennial life span.

fix: 'acute/acuminate at apex': the words 'at apex' set the part, so use the apex instead of the whole blade, as is already done for 'base cuneate'.
reason: The flora says the apex is acute to acuminate, not the whole leaf blade.
9-13 nerves (veins) per leaf, with the leaf as container.
Branchlets are puberulous or glabrous: two alternatives.
'oblong-ovate or oblong': both lie on the oblong-to-ovate range. The 'or oblong' is the oblong end of that range.

target: corolla limb (ligule) of the ray flower
fix: In Asteraceae 'the ray N mm long' after 'Ray florets' means the ligule (the strap-shaped corolla limb), not the whole floret.
reason: The 2-3.5 mm measures the ray (ligule) of the ray floret.

fix: 'anthers absent' inside a female-flower passage (followed by 'Male flowers ...'): put the flower sex in the whole slot.
reason: Anthers are missing only in female flowers. The very next sentence describes the anthers of male flowers.
The interfloral bracts are peltate. 'Bract' is an acceptable part.
'beneath' = the lower (abaxial) side of the blade, which is tomentose. 'Pale' would be a separate colour annotation.
The lower branches are ascending. The 'lower' position slot is filled.

target: floral scale (inflorescence bract) amount 4-6, container = spikelet
fix: A bare count like 'floral scales ... 4-6' within a spikelet description is a count per spikelet. Add the spikelet as container.
reason: 4-6 scales are per spikelet, not for the whole plant or inflorescence.
'subequal' = approximately equal in size.

target: leaf amount 3-4, state = with well-developed blade, container = culm
fix: 'N leaves with X to a culm': both the restriction (with well-developed blades) and the container (culm) are needed.
reason: The count covers only leaves with well-developed blades, per culm. Blade-less basal sheaths are not counted, so a plain 'leaf amount 3-4' is false.
